page: Amazon Web Services m6g.medium is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by a custom 64-bit ARM architecture. It features a single dedicated physical core and vCPU utilizing the AWS Graviton2 processor, specifically the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture operating at 2.5 GHz. The processor is equipped with 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The instance is provisioned with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, does not include local NVMe storage, and lacks integrated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks reflect its single-core, entry-level resource allocation. In stress-ng single-core CPU tests, the instance achieves an average score of 1499.79, though its multi-core scaling is limited by the single-vCPU design. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show read-only speeds of 59.31 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 19.48 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, alongside a write speed of 9.61 GB/sec. In application-level benchmarks, the instance delivers 1.18 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and a static web serving throughput of 1.14 GB/sec. Large language model inference on a small 135M parameter model yields 37.58 tokens per second for prompt processing and 29.07 tokens per second for text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m6g.medium offers a low-cost entry point into the ARM64 ecosystem, providing dedicated CPU resources without the burstable credit constraints of budget-tier instances. However, the single-core limitation presents a performance tradeoff for multi-threaded applications. This instance is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded workloads, basic web serving, development and testing environments, and small-scale Redis caching nodes that do not require high network throughput or local storage.
description: Amazon Web Services m6g.medium is a general-purpose instance featuring a single dedicated vCPU powered by an ARM64 AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It is configured with 4.0 GB of RAM, 32 MB of L3 cache, and operates on the Nitro hypervisor without local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmarks indicate average single-core CPU performance with a stress-ng score of 1499.79, though multi-threaded and memory bandwidth metrics reflect its single-core constraints, showing 19.48 GB/sec uncached read speeds and 9.61 GB/sec write speeds. The instance achieves 1.18 million Redis SET operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 1.14 GB/sec. Qualitatively, it represents a highly cost-efficient option for dedicated ARM64 development, avoiding burstable CPU credits. It is best suited for lightweight web serving, microservices, small caching layers, and single-threaded utility workloads.
